candidates.title: Stilla natt, heliga natt
candidates.first_line: Stilla natt, heliga natt, över jord gjuter
candidates.notes: Mannström born 1875, died 1938 (sv.wikipedia). Translation dated 1915 (sv.wikipedia; sv.wikisource lists 'Stilla natt (Mannström)' 1915). Alternative pre-1931 version: Edvard Evers (1853-1919), adaptation 1917, same article. The commonly sung text is the Torsten Fogelqvist (1880-1941) 1937 revision, which still meets the 1955 rule. Joseph Mohr's death year was not in any fetched source, so lyricist_died is null. The first line comes from the hymnary URL slug, not from quoted lyrics, so verify it. The title is in the first five words, so this round is too easy: alt_words is still needed. Take a 5-word run from verse 1, line 2 of the Mannström text. Sources do not give Mannström's exact publication date beyond the 1915 translation date.

candidates.title: Ett barn är fött på denna dag
candidates.first_line: Ett barn är fött på denna dag
candidates.notes: Based on Luther's 'Vom Himmel hoch'. Olaus Martini (d. 1609) wrote the Swedish text, dated 1617 in print. Wallin (1779-1839, sv.wikipedia) reworked it in 1817. Samuel Ödmann also reworked it early; his dates were not verified, so check whether his version is the one sung before using it. The sv.wikipedia article gives a 1913 publication for the song in Kyrklig sång. The first line matches the article title (fetched metadata). Sources disagree on whether Martini or Luther wrote the Swedish text (singpraises.net names Luther). Wallin's entry on sv.wikipedia was truncated before the hymn list, so his credit for this hymn is taken from the Ett barn article.

candidates.title: Det är en ros utsprungen
candidates.lyricist: unverified (German original 'Es ist ein Ros entsprungen')
candidates.notes: Thekla Knös (1815-1880) credited as translator on sv.wikipedia, translation dated 1867. Sv.wikipedia gives first Swedish printing as the 1921 Swedish psalmbok, and the 1937 hymnbook as no. 51. Hymnary.org lists the translator as anonymous, so the attribution is disputed. Fetched metadata for the first line matches the title, so the five words are the title: alt_words is needed and was not obtained. Lyricist of the German original is not verified; the lyricist field is left as a placeholder. Check the original author before using this. Lower-confidence candidate.
